source.text: Two fractions represent the same quantity when they describe the same proportion of a whole. Multiplying or dividing the numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number changes the representation but preserves the value. In this fixture, 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent.
source.provenance: Created inside Learning App Round 7 QA on 2026-09-30; synthetic test content.

objective: Explain why 1/2 and 2/4 represent an equal quantity.
orientation: Two different-looking fractions. The question is whether they describe the same part of one whole.

teaching.text: A whole can be split into equal parts. 1/2 is 1 of 2 equal parts.
2/4 is 2 of 4 equal parts of the same whole.
Multiplying numerator and denominator by the same number, here 2, changes the representation but keeps the same proportion. So 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent.

challenge.prompt: Explain why 1/2 and 2/4 represent the same quantity.

responses.STRONG: Numerator and denominator of 1/2 are both multiplied by 2, so 2/4 describes the same proportion of the whole.
responses.PARTIAL: 1/2 = 2/4. The shaded parts match, but I can't say why.
responses.MISCONCEPTION: 2/4 is larger, because 2 and 4 are larger than 1 and 2.

STRONG.feedback: You explained the common scaling and the unchanged proportion.
STRONG.next_action: Continue: test the same relation on another pair.

PARTIAL.feedback: Your representation is right: the shaded parts match. The reason is still missing.
PARTIAL.hint: Compare how the numerator and the denominator changed from 1/2 to 2/4.
PARTIAL.repair_prompt: What was done to both the numerator and the denominator to get from 1/2 to 2/4?

MISCONCEPTION.feedback: Your answer compares the size of the numbers, not the part of the whole.
MISCONCEPTION.corrective: Larger numbers do not mean a larger quantity here. The shaded part of 2/4 covers exactly the same extent of the whole as 1/2.
MISCONCEPTION.repair_prompt: Look at the two bars. Does 2/4 cover more of the whole than 1/2, or the same?
MISCONCEPTION.next_action: Corrective teaching, then a smaller comparison check.
